title: Creation stories around the world
examples: How do different faiths tell the story of creation?
What does Genesis say about creation?
Can you believe in the Big Bang and in God?

explain.say: Every culture has asked where the world and people came from. Creation stories answer in many beautiful ways, and for believers they also say why we are here and how we should live.

draw.text: Where did everything come from? Why are we here?

explain.say: Genesis, the first book of the Jewish and Christian Bible, tells how God created the world in six days and rested on the seventh. The Quran also speaks of the heavens and earth being created in six days, which many Muslims understand as long periods.

draw.text: Day 7: God rests, the root of the Sabbath

explain.say: Many Hindu traditions see time as vast cycles: the universe is created, kept and dissolved, again and again, linked with Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. The Rigveda's Hymn of Creation even wonders whether anyone truly knows how it began.

draw.text: One day of Brahma, a kalpa, is said to last 4.32 billion years

explain.say: Around the world there are many more stories. In Norse myth the world is made from the body of the first giant, Ymir; in China, Pangu pushes apart the sky and the earth; in ancient Egypt, the first land rises from endless dark water.

draw.label: Some places whose creation stories we know

draw.text: Norse: Ymir. Chinese: Pangu. Egyptian: the first mound

explain.say: Many stories share patterns: order coming out of chaos or water, a cosmic egg, sky and earth pushed apart, as in the Maori story of Rangi and Papa, and the world shaped by ancestors, as in the Aboriginal Australian Dreaming.

items: Out of water or chaos: Egypt, Genesis
A cosmic egg: Pangu, Hindu texts
Sky and earth parted: Maori, Pangu

explain.say: Science explains origins with evidence: the universe began expanding in the Big Bang about 13.8 billion years ago, and Earth formed about 4.5 billion years ago. Many religious people see science and sacred stories as answering different questions, how and why.

items: 13.8 billion years ago: the Big Bang
4.6 billion: the Sun and Earth form

draw.text: The Big Bang idea was first proposed by Georges Lemaitre, a Catholic priest and physicist

faq.q: How do different faiths tell the story of creation?
faq.a: Judaism and Christianity tell, in Genesis, of God creating the world in six days; the Quran also speaks of creation in six days, or periods; many Hindu traditions describe endless cycles of creation and dissolution. Other cultures, from the Norse to the Maori, have their own stories.
asks: What are some creation stories?
How do religions explain how the world began?
Compare creation stories of different religions

faq.q: What does Genesis say about creation?
faq.a: Genesis chapter 1 tells how God created light, sky, land, plants, sun, moon and stars, creatures and people over six days, and rested on the seventh. Chapter 2 tells a second, closer story, of God forming Adam from the dust and placing him in the Garden of Eden with Eve.
asks: What is the Bible creation story?
What happened on each day of creation?
Who were Adam and Eve?

faq.q: What does the Quran say about creation?
faq.a: The Quran says God created the heavens and the earth in six days, which many Muslims understand as long periods, and that when God wills something, he says Be, and it is. It tells that Adam, the first human, was created from clay.
asks: What is the Islamic creation story?
How did God create the world in Islam?
What does kun fayakun mean?

faq.q: What is the Hindu view of creation?
faq.a: Many Hindu traditions see the universe as going through endless cycles of creation, preservation and dissolution, linked with Brahma the creator, Vishnu the preserver and Shiva the destroyer. One day of Brahma, called a kalpa, is said to last 4.32 billion years.
asks: What do Hindus believe about how the world began?
What is a kalpa?
Does Hinduism have a creation story?

faq.q: What is the Hymn of Creation in the Rigveda?
faq.a: The Nasadiya Sukta, in the tenth book of the Rigveda, imagines a time before existence and non-existence. It ends by wondering whether even the one who oversees it all knows how creation began, perhaps he knows, or perhaps he does not.
asks: What is the Nasadiya Sukta?
Does the Rigveda talk about creation?
Which ancient text questions creation?

faq.q: Does Buddhism have a creation story?
faq.a: The Buddha did not teach a story of how the universe was first created. He set aside questions such as whether the world is eternal, comparing them to a man struck by an arrow who wants to know everything about the archer before letting it be pulled out.
asks: What do Buddhists believe about creation?
Did the Buddha talk about how the world began?
What is the parable of the arrow?

faq.q: What is the Norse creation story?
faq.a: In Norse myth, between a land of fire and a land of ice lay a great emptiness, Ginnungagap. From melting ice came the giant Ymir, and the god Odin and his brothers made the world from his body: the earth from his flesh and the sky from his skull.
asks: Who is Ymir?
How did the Vikings think the world began?
What is Ginnungagap?

faq.a: In a Chinese creation story, Pangu grows inside a cosmic egg and then pushes the sky and the earth apart, holding them for thousands of years. When he dies, his body becomes the mountains, rivers, sun and moon, and in another story the goddess Nuwa shapes people from clay.
asks: What is the Chinese creation story?
Who is Nuwa?
What is the cosmic egg story?

faq.q: What is the Maori creation story?
faq.a: In Maori tradition, Ranginui, the sky father, and Papatuanuku, the earth mother, held each other so tightly that their children lived in darkness. Their son Tane pushed them apart, letting light into the world.
asks: Who are Rangi and Papa?
How did the world begin in Maori stories?
Who is Tane?

faq.a: For Aboriginal Australians, the Dreaming describes how ancestral beings shaped the land, animals, people and laws, and it is linked to particular places in the landscape. It is not only about the past but continues in the present, through stories, song, dance and art.
asks: What is the Dreamtime?
What do Aboriginal Australians believe about creation?
What are Dreaming stories?

faq.q: What is the ancient Egyptian creation story?
faq.a: In one Egyptian story, at first there was only Nun, a dark endless ocean. A mound of land rose from the water, and the creator god Atum appeared on it and began to create the other gods and the world.
asks: How did the Egyptians think the world began?
Who is Atum?
What is Nun in Egyptian myth?

faq.q: What does science say about how the universe began?
faq.a: Scientists find, from evidence such as the expansion of the universe and the leftover glow of the early universe, that it began in a hot, dense state about 13.8 billion years ago, called the Big Bang. Earth formed about 4.5 billion years ago, and life evolved over billions of years.
asks: What is the Big Bang?
How old is the universe?
How did life begin according to science?

faq.q: Can you believe in the Big Bang and in God?
faq.a: Many people do. Georges Lemaitre, a Catholic priest and physicist, first proposed the idea that became the Big Bang theory, and many believers see science explaining how the world works while faith speaks of why. Others read their creation story literally, and some people hold no religious belief.
asks: Do religion and science disagree about creation?
Are creation stories true?
Who came up with the Big Bang?

faq.q: What do creation stories have in common?
faq.a: Many begin with water, darkness or chaos, then bring order: light appears, sky and earth separate, and land, creatures and people follow. Many also explain why people should live in a certain way.
asks: Why are creation stories similar?
What themes appear in creation myths?
Are all creation stories alike?

facts: In Genesis chapter 1, God creates the world in six days and rests on the seventh.
The Rigveda's Nasadiya Sukta, the Hymn of Creation, ends by wondering whether anyone truly knows how creation began.
In Norse myth the world is made from the body of the first giant, Ymir.
Scientists estimate the universe began in the Big Bang about 13.8 billion years ago, and Earth formed about 4.5 billion years ago.
Georges Lemaitre, a Catholic priest and physicist, first proposed the idea that became the Big Bang theory, in 1927.

quiz.say: In which tradition does the world come from the body of a giant named Ymir?
quiz.show: Whose creation story features the giant Ymir?
quiz.why: In Norse myth, Odin and his brothers made the world from the body of the first giant, Ymir.

wrong.1: The Maori story tells of Rangi and Papa, the sky and earth, pushed apart by Tane.
wrong.2: The Egyptian story begins with a mound of land rising from the dark waters of Nun.
wrong.3: The Chinese story with a giant is about Pangu, not Ymir, though the two are alike.

quiz.say: Genesis, the Maori story and the Pangu story all describe separating something. What is it?

options.show: Sky and earth, or the waters
options.say: The sky and the earth, or the waters above and below

quiz.why: A common pattern is the parting of sky and earth, or of the waters, to make room for light and life.

wrong.1: Fire and ice appear in the Norse story, but they meet rather than being separated.
wrong.2: That is not a pattern in these stories.

quiz.say: Many believers accept the Big Bang and still value their creation story. How can both fit together?
quiz.show: How can science and a creation story fit together?

options.show: They answer different questions: how and why
options.say: They answer different questions, how and why

quiz.why: Many people see science explaining how the universe developed, and sacred stories speaking about meaning, purpose and why we are here.

wrong.1: The Big Bang is supported by strong evidence, such as the expanding universe.
wrong.2: Most believers read creation stories for meaning rather than as scientific reports.
